PLPC is a low-attention small-cap conductor and pole-line hardware candidate; prioritize verification of U.S. utility/transmission revenue mix and order trends.

POWL should be tracked as a direct switchgear/electrical power systems candidate with strong backlog signals, but its market cap has moved slightly above the preferred underfollowed $300M-$10B range.

AZZ is a high-quality second-order underfollowed candidate because galvanizing for T&D structures, monopoles and lattice towers may benefit from grid buildout while being hidden under coatings/industrial-services labels.

WCC is a distributor/logistics candidate for transformer, switchgear, T&D hardware and data-center electrical products; later layers should validate whether backlog and supplier allocation create pricing power or only pass-through revenue.

HUBB is the reference benchmark for direct grid-component exposure, with Utility Solutions at 63% of 2025 revenue and products spanning transmission, distribution, substation, grid controls and utility meters.

POWL should remain in the underfollowed grid-switchgear lane; it has direct medium-voltage electrical distribution exposure, utility growth, data-center order evidence, and backlog disclosures.
PLPC is a narrower conductor/transmission-hardware shadow candidate; evidence is weaker than POWL or MYRG and requires direct filing verification before advancing beyond Layer 1.

MYRG expands the node from equipment manufacturing into execution capacity: T&D construction labor, substations, distribution MSAs, and data-center electrical contracting may become bottleneck proxies.
GE Vernova should be used as the reference anchor for grid-equipment backlog, transformer/switchgear demand, and large-customer order-cycle validation, not as the main underfollowed discovery asset.

Need a follow-up pass for transformer-component suppliers, copper/aluminum conductor suppliers, protection relays, testing/certification labs, and distributor channels; current pass is biased toward public companies with easily visible backlog disclosures.

node: Grid transformers, high-voltage equipment, switchgear, and conductors
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the grid equipment chokepoint using a two-lane funnel. Reference lane: Hubbell as a larger, obvious utility T&D component leader. Underfollowed/discovery lane: Powell Industries for medium-voltage switchgear and backlog sensitivity, Preformed Line Products for conductor/pole-line hardware, and Atkore for electrical infrastructure products tied to data-center, solar, industrial, and electrification demand. These are research candidates only, not recommendations. Expanded the node around U.S.-listed grid equipment and second-order infrastructure suppliers. The strongest underfollowed lane candidates are Powell Industries for medium-voltage switchgear and electrical power systems backlog, AZZ for corrosion-protection/galvanizing exposure to transmission and distribution steel structures, and Wesco for utility/data-center electrical distribution and supply-chain visibility. Hubbell is included as a larger reference anchor because its Utility Solutions segment has unusually direct exposure to transmission, distribution, substation, grid controls, meters, arresters, insulators, connectors, bushings, cutouts and switches. No buy/sell view is implied. Layer 1B expansion for the grid-equipment chokepoint favors a two-lane universe: GE Vernova as a reference anchor for grid-equipment backlog and electrification demand, plus underfollowed public suppliers and contractors where backlog, utility qualification, or niche transmission/distribution exposure may reveal second-order benefits before utilities or renewable developers show clean ea
